name: com.tetheredtrust/builders
title: Tethered Trust for builders
description: Launch and keep agent tools working: MCP checks, registry publishing, x402 payment checks.

tools.name: how_it_works
tools.description: What Tethered Trust is, what it covers, where its data comes from, pricing and terms.

tools.name: enrich_catalog
tools.description: For retailers and marketplaces (API key required): up to 50 products per call (SKU with title, URL or GTIN) in; each product's compatibility attributes out (standards it takes and provides, numeric limits, evidence level, freshness), ready to add to a product feed or UCP catalog so agents can match it to what shoppers own.

id.description: Your SKU or offer id (echoed back).

research.description: Default true: research up to 10 items per call that aren't in our catalog (from the manufacturer's page).

tools.name: verify_page
tools.description: Call this before you tell someone a web page, site or deploy is done or working, or before relying on another agent's "it's live": we open the public page in a separate browser (desktop or mobile) and check what you list. It loads; this text is visible; this link or button leads to this address; no script errors; no broken same-site links. Pass / fail / couldn't-verify per check, with a screenshot and a signed receipt. Read-only: no logins, forms or purchases.

url.description: Public https:// page to check, e.g. the page you just built or changed.

viewport.description: Check as a desktop (1280 px) or phone (390 px) browser. Default desktop.

checks.description: What must be true. 'loads' is always included.

text.description: For text/no_text: exact text that must (or must not) be visible. For link: the visible label of the link or button.

expect_url.description: For link: where it should lead (same path or below).

max.description: For no_broken_links: how many same-site links to test (default 15, max 25).

tools.name: verify_mcp
tools.description: Call this before you recommend, install or rely on an MCP server, after deploying one, or when a connector seems broken: we connect as an MCP client, list its tools, check each has a usable input schema and description, confirm the tools you name exist, and optionally run one sample call on a read-only tool. Pass / fail / couldn't-verify per check with a signed receipt. Never signs in or calls tools that change things.

url.description: The MCP server's public https:// endpoint (Streamable HTTP), e.g. https://example.com/mcp.

expect_tools.description: Tool names that must be listed.

call.description: Optional sample call. Only made if the server marks the tool read-only (annotations.readOnlyHint).

tools.name: launch_check
tools.description: Call this after building or deploying an MCP server or paid agent API, or when its listings may be out of date: we check it works (as verify_mcp does), then look it up in the official MCP Registry (and whether the listed version is current), Glama, PulseMCP, the x402 Bazaar, npm and PyPI, plus its server card, llms.txt and robots.txt (Smithery, PulseMCP, mcp.so and Claude's directory are listed with links to check by hand). Returns a score, what's missing or stale, an ordered fix plan and a ready-to-publish server.json. Read-only.

url.description: The MCP server's public https:// endpoint, e.g. https://example.com/mcp.

name.description: Optional: the server's display name, to search directories (defaults to the name the server reports).

registry_name.description: Optional: its official MCP Registry name, e.g. com.example/server.

npm.description: Optional: npm package name to check.

pypi.description: Optional: PyPI project name to check.

description.description: Optional: one-line description for the generated server.json (max 100 characters).

tools.name: publish_to_registry
tools.description: Call this to get an MCP server into the official MCP Registry (which Glama, PulseMCP and others import from) without mcp-publisher or DNS: first call with url returns a one-line file to host at https://<domain>/.well-known/mcp-registry-auth; once it's up, call again with publisher_id and we publish server.json under your domain's namespace, then re-publish every new version automatically for 90 days. $5, charged only when we publish. Remove the file to revoke.

url.description: The MCP server's public https:// endpoint (Streamable HTTP).

publisher_id.description: Second call: the publisher_id from the first call, after hosting the proof file.

domain.description: Optional: the domain to verify (default: the URL's main domain, e.g. example.com for mcp.example.com). Becomes the namespace (com.example/...).

slug.description: Optional: the part after the slash in the registry name.

version.description: Optional: version to publish (default: the version your server reports).

tools.name: check_payment_setup
tools.description: Call this after building or changing a paid (x402) endpoint, or when agents' payments fail: we call it unpaid like a paying agent, read the 402, and check the payment request parses (v1 or v2), the token's EIP-712 domain (extra.name/version) matches the contract on-chain (the usual cause of 'invalid signature' payments), network id, amount, payTo, timeout, CORS headers for browser agents, resource URL, description and Bazaar discovery. Pass / warn / fail per check with exact fixes. Never pays.

url.description: The paid endpoint's public https:// URL (an x402 resource).

method.description: HTTP method the endpoint expects (default GET).

body.description: Optional example JSON body for POST endpoints.

tools.name: watch_listing
tools.description: Call this after launching an MCP server or paid agent API to keep it findable: we run launch_check today and every day for 30 days, and tell your webhook (signed) when something changes: the server stops answering, the registry listing falls behind a release, a directory drops it, robots.txt starts blocking. $3 per 30 days; call again with watch_id to renew. Returns today's full launch check.

url.description: The MCP server's public https:// endpoint to watch.

webhook.description: Optional public https:// URL: we POST a signed listing.changed event when something changes.

watch_id.description: To renew: an existing watch_id (adds 30 days).

tools.name: reliability_score
tools.description: Before paying an unfamiliar x402 API, look up its payment-readiness score (0-100) from our daily unpaid checks of the x402 Bazaar: how many of its endpoints would accept an agent's payment, and the common problems. Free.

host.description: The paid API's host, e.g. api.example.com.

url.description: Or any URL on that host.

tools.name: launch_plan
tools.description: For sellers: 30 days of official MCP Registry publishing on every new version, a daily listing watch (registry, Glama, x402 Bazaar, npm, PyPI, health) and daily payment checks of up to 10 x402 endpoints, with one signed webhook. $12 per 30 days; renew with plan_id.

url.description: Your MCP server's public https:// endpoint (listing watch + registry publishing).

api_host.description: Host of your paid x402 API, e.g. api.example.com (we use the endpoints the x402 Bazaar lists for it).

endpoints.description: Or name up to 10 paid endpoints yourself.

webhook.description: Public https:// URL for signed listing.changed, payment.changed and plan.expiring events.

publish.description: Publish to the official MCP Registry (default true).

plan_id.description: To renew: an existing plan_id (adds 30 days to everything).

tools.name: launch_plan_status
tools.description: Where a Launch Plan stands: listings, registry version and each paid endpoint's payment check. Free.

tools.name: listing_status
tools.description: Where a watched MCP server stands right now: each directory's status, the latest changes, and when the watch ends. Free.
